accepted_design_constraints.title: Recoverable non-atomic worktree branch switch
accepted_design_constraints.problem: git worktree branch switch is not an atomic transaction; disk exhaustion, permission failure or process termination may leave observable intermediate state.

precheck: worktree is clean including staged, unstaged and untracked files
no Git operation such as merge, rebase, cherry-pick, bisect or sequencer is active
original and target symbolic refs and expected OIDs are observed
worktree and gitdir permissions are writable
worktree and gitdir filesystems each satisfy required_free_bytes=max(512MiB,1.5*estimated_checkout_write_bytes); estimation failure is fail-closed
required_protocol.intent: persist operation/attempt ID, project, worktree path, original branch/OID, target branch/OID, expected integration OID and phase outside the target worktree before invoking git switch
required_protocol.postcheck: command exit success is insufficient; re-observe symbolic HEAD, HEAD OID, worktree registration and clean status before VERIFIED/PASS
required_protocol.failure_observation: after any error or interruption, re-observe actual repository state and never infer the current branch from the last attempted step
required_protocol.conditional_rollback: automatic return to integration is allowed only when the worktree is clean, no Git operation is active, original integration ref/OID has not drifted, and permission/space prechecks pass again
required_protocol.unsafe_recovery: otherwise preserve the worktree and CR branch, set RECOVERY_REQUIRED/BLOCKED, and emit observation-based manual recovery guidance
required_protocol.idempotency: resume/recover must be re-runnable and may only report already-recovered, recovery-in-progress or still-blocked based on fresh observations

cp3_acceptance: HLD, ADR, state machine and failure-path simulation explicitly consume this constraint
CP3 must not claim git switch itself is atomic
uncertain state cannot be reported as integration-idle or PASS

architecture_gray_area_candidates: metadata/path schema, portable anchors and control-vs-project-worktree ownership
heterogeneous source-default/artifact-integration leg commands, expected OIDs and cleanup
leg result/aggregate result correlation, single-writer ledger and receipt/OID self-reference avoidance
integration create-only bootstrap CAS, remote-ref race and idempotency
CR-external manual main/integration synchronization precheck, direction, mutual exclusion and recovery
aggregate resume/abort after partial success without automatic rollback or close
non_authorized: real artifact migration or symlink mutation
real worktree, branch, ref, commit or remote mutation
credentials, runtime, SaaS, production write, publish or trading
